## File tree {.i-tree-view}

When you open the Files Panel, the file tree is shown with its root folder expanded. Folders and files are drawn with [Catppuccin's file icons](https://catppuccin.com). If the project is a git repository, its changes are shown on the folders and files. The file tree supports mouse dragging and common keyboard shortcuts.

## File preview & editing {.i-file-text}

Click a file to open it in a pane between the tree and the chat; click it again to close it. The enlarge button gives the pane the chat's room. You can use common keyboard shortcuts to undo, redo, save, and close.

Emaki supports format on save for common languages. It is off by default and can be turned on in [Settings](settings.qmd): tick all the languages, or only the ones you want.

Supported file types:

::: {.types}
- [Code]{.t-code}
- [Markdown]{.t-markdown}
- [CSV and TSV]{.t-csv}
- [Parquet]{.t-parquet}
- [Word]{.t-word}
- [Excel]{.t-excel}
- [PowerPoint]{.t-powerpoint}
- [PDF]{.t-pdf}
- [HTML]{.t-html}
- [Pictures]{.t-pictures}
:::

## Git {.i-git-branch}

If the project is a git repository, the git buttons appear in the Files Panel's header. Click the branch name to switch branches or create a new one ([⌘⇧N]{.kbd}). You can also fetch, pull, and publish from there.

The **Changes** pill ([⌘⇧G]{.kbd}) opens the Changes sheet. There you can review your changes, write a commit message, commit ([⌘↩]{.kbd}), and push ([⌘P]{.kbd}). The sheet's **History** side lists your past commits.
